Definition: to draw, used in a great variety of applications (including to sow, to sound, to prolong, to develop, to march, to remove, to delay, to be tall, etc.)
BiblicalUsage: mâshak is to draw, and it is used for a bow, a yoke, a plough, and a melody. In 1 Kings 22:34 and 2 Chronicles 18:33 a man draws a bow at a venture and smites the king of Israel between the joints of the harness. In Deuteronomy 21:3 the heifer has not drawn in the yoke, and in Amos 9:13 the hills shall melt, drawn out like wax. The word is pulling, and what is pulled can be a weapon or a harvest.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mâshak shows me that drawing can be gentle or violent. I hold that the same God who draws a bow in judgment draws me with cords of love.
RelatedTopics: God's Sovereignty; Judgment; Love of God
